list_desktop_windows.name: list_desktop_windows
list_desktop_windows.description: List all visible top-level desktop windows on the system (HWND, PID, title, geometry). Use this before capture_desktop_window to find target window title or HWND.

capture_desktop_window.name: capture_desktop_window
capture_desktop_window.description: Capture a screenshot of a specific desktop window by its title substring or numeric HWND. Safe targeted capture using Win32 API.

capture_desktop_screen.name: capture_desktop_screen
capture_desktop_screen.description: Capture a screenshot of the entire desktop screen (primary monitor or all virtual monitors). Useful for fullscreen games, Unity Play Mode, or overall desktop view.

get_clipboard_image.name: get_clipboard_image
get_clipboard_image.description: Retrieve an image or screenshot currently stored in the system clipboard (e.g. copied via Win+Shift+S, PrintScreen, or image copy).

create_artifact.name: create_artifact
create_artifact.description: Create a Markdown artifact in the .argent/artifacts/ directory. Useful for documenting plans, research, or long text.

request_user_approval.name: request_user_approval
request_user_approval.description: Pause execution and wait for the user to explicitly approve a plan or action. Use this before making major changes.

call_mcp_tool.name: call_mcp_tool
call_mcp_tool.description: Call a tool on an external MCP server (Unity Editor, GitHub, Slack, a database…). The servers connected right now are listed in the MCP SERVERS section of your instructions. If you do not know the exact tool name or its arguments, call list_mcp_tools first — guessing a signature wastes a turn.

list_mcp_tools.name: list_mcp_tools
list_mcp_tools.description:
Look up what an MCP server can do. A single server can expose well over a hundred tools, so their signatures are NOT in your instructions — you fetch the ones you need, when you need them.
  list_mcp_tools() — which servers exist and how many tools each has
  list_mcp_tools('unity', 'navmesh') — signatures of the matching tools
Filter by what you are trying to do ('scene', 'animation', 'build'); an unfiltered list on a big server gives names only.

run_subagent.name: run_subagent
run_subagent.description: Spawn a specialized sub-agent to handle a specific part of a complex task in isolation. This is great for research, code reviews, or implementing small isolated modules.

read_file.name: read_file
read_file.description: Reads file content. Every line is prefixed with its line number and a tab — that gutter is NOT part of the file: never include it in target_text or in content you write back. Long files are truncated; use start_line/end_line to read specific sections.

write_file.name: write_file
write_file.description: Writes content to a file. WARNING: DO NOT USE THIS TO EDIT EXISTING FILES >150 LINES! It will be blocked to prevent truncation. Use replace_in_file or multi_replace_in_file instead. This tool is ONLY for creating NEW files or writing very small scripts.

list_skills.name: list_skills
list_skills.description: Lists all available markdown-based skills. Use this to discover specialized instructions you or the user have created.

read_skill.name: read_skill
read_skill.description: Reads the full instructions of a specific skill. Use this to follow complex workflows or expert guidelines. SKILL.md folder skills also list bundled scripts/references/assets and their folder path — read or run those with read_file / run_command when the instructions call for them.

replace_in_file.name: replace_in_file
replace_in_file.description: Replaces a specific text block in a file with new content. Use this to edit existing files without rewriting them entirely. The target text must be a unique, exact match.

delete_file.name: delete_file
delete_file.description: Deletes a file from the file system.

create_directory.name: create_directory
create_directory.description: Creates a new directory and all parent directories if needed.

move_file.name: move_file
move_file.description: Moves or renames a file from one path to another.

copy_file.name: copy_file
copy_file.description: Copies a file from one path to another. Creates parent directories if needed.

list_directory.name: list_directory
list_directory.description: Lists all files and subdirectories within a given directory.

search_files.name: search_files
search_files.description: Recursively search for files matching specific criteria. Use this to find files by pattern (e.g., *.cs), by name, or by content without requiring user confirmation.

grep_search.name: grep_search
grep_search.description: Search file or directory contents using a regex pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Faster and more precise than search_files for finding specific code, function calls, or text patterns.

run_command.name: run_command
run_command.description: Runs a CLI shell command on the user's system and returns the stdout and stderr. Always prefer non-interactive flags (e.g. `npx -y ...`, `npm init -y`, `pip install --no-input ...`, `--no-pager`) so tools do not hang awaiting interactive input.

run_admin_command.name: run_admin_command
run_admin_command.description: Runs a PowerShell command with Administrator privileges. This triggers a Windows UAC prompt for the user. Use this only when you explicitly need elevated permissions (e.g., editing registry, setting global system variables, installing system-wide services).

search_web.name: search_web
search_web.description:
Searches the web across several engines at once (DuckDuckGo, Wikipedia, StackOverflow, GitHub issues, and Brave when configured) and merges the results.
Search operators are supported and worth using — each engine is automatically given only the ones it understands:
  "exact phrase"  — the words must appear together, verbatim. The single most effective technique for error messages: "NullReferenceException in LoadAsync".
  site:docs.unity3d.com  — restrict to one domain (vendor docs, a specific forum).
  filetype:pdf  — restrict to a file type (also ext:).
  -word  — exclude results containing it, e.g. -tutorial to skip beginner pages.
  intitle:word  — the word must be in the TITLE, not merely mentioned. Use it when a common term drowns in passing mentions; it is translated to each engine's native form (GitHub's in:title, StackOverflow's title filter).
Combine them: 'site:forum.unity.com "Addressables" memory leak -tutorial'.
Quoted phrases work everywhere; the rest are applied where the engine supports them and dropped where it does not, so writing them is never harmful.
WARNING: this returns only short snippets and URLs. To read the actual content, you MUST call `read_webpage` with the returned URL.

read_webpage.name: read_webpage
read_webpage.description: Reads and extracts the main text content from a specific webpage URL. Use this to dive deeper into results found via search_web.

start_background_command.name: start_background_command
start_background_command.description: Starts a command in the background (e.g. dev servers, infinite loops) and returns a PID. Use this instead of run_command for long-running processes.

analyze_project.name: analyze_project
analyze_project.description: Analyze the current project structure in one call: directory tree, detected languages/frameworks, entry points, build/test commands and file statistics. Use this FIRST when onboarding to a codebase or writing/updating AGENTS.md.

list_background_commands.name: list_background_commands
list_background_commands.description: List the background processes you started this session, with their PID, status (running/exited) and command. Use this to recover a PID you forgot before reading output or stopping a process.

read_background_command.name: read_background_command
read_background_command.description: Reads newer output (stdout/stderr) from a currently running background process by PID. If there is no new output, do NOT keep calling this in a loop — use wait_heartbeat(until='process_finished("PID")') to sleep until the process finishes, or proceed with other work.

send_background_command.name: send_background_command
send_background_command.description: Sends string input to the stdin of a running background process. Use this to interact with REPLs or commands waiting for input.

get_file_outline.name: get_file_outline
get_file_outline.description: Get the structural outline (classes and methods) of a Python (.py) or C# (.cs) file without reading the entire file body. Ideal for exploring large projects.

multi_replace_in_file.name: multi_replace_in_file
multi_replace_in_file.description: Perform multiple target/replacement edits across one or several files in a single tool call.

read_git_diff.name: read_git_diff
read_git_diff.description: Read the current unstaged and staged Git differences in the project. Use this to understand what has changed compared to the last commit.

run_deep_research.name: run_deep_research
run_deep_research.description: Starts an autonomous Deep Research Sub-Agent that deeply researches an objective using search engines, reads top web pages, extracts data, and returns a massive synthesized technical report. Use this instead of search_web for broad topics. You can guide the research with focus/context parameters and control depth with max_rounds.

find_definition.name: find_definition
find_definition.description: Find the definition of a class, function, or variable at a specific line and column. Use this instead of grep for precise navigation.

find_references.name: find_references
find_references.description: Find all usages (references) of a symbol at a specific line and column.

git_checkpoint.name: git_checkpoint
git_checkpoint.description: Create a temporary git commit to save current progress. Use this before making risky changes or running experiments.

git_rollback.name: git_rollback
git_rollback.description: Revert all changes to an 'Argent Checkpoint'. Use this if an experiment failed, logic is broken beyond simple repair, or the user asks to undo/return to an earlier state. Argent auto-creates a checkpoint before the first edit of each turn, so recent states are usually available.

calculate.name: calculate
calculate.description: Evaluates exact arithmetic or symbolic math expressions (e.g. arithmetic, trigonometry, calculus, algebra) and returns the result.

ask_user_questions.name: ask_user_questions
ask_user_questions.description: Ask the user a series of structured questions. Use this when you need clarification, preferences, or decisions on multiple points before proceeding.

wait_heartbeat.name: wait_heartbeat
wait_heartbeat.description:
Pause execution while something finishes: a compilation, a server starting, a long background task.
IMPORTANT: Do NOT use wait_heartbeat for web pages or browser tasks (such as file/video upload or page loading) — it only monitors local filesystem files and background OS processes. For browser and web tasks, you MUST use browser_wait_for instead.
PREFER `until`: waking up costs a full turn, so polling 'is it done yet?' ten times costs ten turns, while a condition is checked locally for free and wakes you once — when it actually happened. Fall back to `delay_seconds` only when nothing observable marks the end.
Checks available to `until`: file_exists(path), file_missing(path), file_contains(path, text), process_finished(pid), process_running(pid). Combine them with and / or / not.
Examples:
  until='file_contains("build.log", "BUILD SUCCESSFUL")'
  until='process_finished("3")', timeout_seconds=1200
  until='file_exists("dist/app.exe") and file_missing(".lock")'
You are told whether the condition was MET or the wait TIMED OUT — a timeout is not success, so re-check before assuming the event happened.

view_image.name: view_image
view_image.description:
LOOK at an image file — a screenshot, a mockup, a diagram, a photo the user pointed at. Use it when the answer depends on what something LOOKS like: verifying a layout you just changed, reading a chart, checking a rendered page.
The image arrives in the NEXT message, not in this tool's result, so continue after calling it and describe what you actually see. Do not claim to have seen anything before that.
Text is still cheaper: for the CONTENT of a web page use read_webpage.

browser_open.name: browser_open
browser_open.description: Open a URL in the built-in browser. Creates a browser session if needed. By default, automatically returns the updated page state (URL, title, and interactive elements) so you don't need a separate browser_state call.

browser_state.name: browser_state
browser_state.description: Get the current state of the browser page: URL, title, and a numbered list of all interactive elements. Can be filtered by a query keyword.

browser_click.name: browser_click
browser_click.description: Click on an element. You must specify either the index (from browser_state), a CSS selector, or the visible text of the element. By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_input.name: browser_input
browser_input.description: Type text into an input field or textarea. You must specify either the index (from browser_state) or a CSS selector to target the input. By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_select.name: browser_select
browser_select.description: Select an option in a <select> dropdown by index, selector, value, or visible label. By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_screenshot.name: browser_screenshot
browser_screenshot.description: Take a screenshot of the current browser page and save it to disk. Returns the file path of the saved image.

browser_scroll.name: browser_scroll
browser_scroll.description: Scroll the browser page up, down, left, right, or scroll a specific element into view. By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_wait_for.name: browser_wait_for
browser_wait_for.description: Wait for an element matching text/CSS selector or a JavaScript expression to satisfy a state on the page. Use this to wait for file/video upload completion, page transitions, dynamic content, or button activation (e.g. state='enabled'). Automatically returns the fresh page state once ready, eliminating blind polling loops and replacing wait_heartbeat for browser tasks.

browser_get_content.name: browser_get_content
browser_get_content.description: Extract content from the current browser page. Can return plain text, markdown, or raw HTML. Use 'text' for body text, 'markdown' for structured readable content, 'html' for raw source. Use 'text', 'selector', or 'index' to target a specific part/element/card of the page.

browser_close.name: browser_close
browser_close.description: Close a browser session and free resources. Always close sessions when done with browser automation.

browser_switch_tab.name: browser_switch_tab
browser_switch_tab.description: Switch the active tab/page of a named browser session by its 1-based index (e.g. 1, 2). Use this to switch focus when a link opened a new tab.

browser_press_key.name: browser_press_key
browser_press_key.description: Press a keyboard key in the browser (e.g. 'Enter', 'Escape', 'Tab', 'ArrowDown', 'Backspace', 'PageDown'). By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_fill_form.name: browser_fill_form
browser_fill_form.description: Batch-fill multiple form fields and optionally submit the form in a single turn. Dramatically saves steps when logging in or filling forms.

browser_upload_file.name: browser_upload_file
browser_upload_file.description: Upload a local file to a file input element (<input type="file">). By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_back.name: browser_back
browser_back.description: Navigate back to the previous page in history. By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_reload.name: browser_reload
browser_reload.description: Reload the current page. By default, automatically returns the updated page state.

browser_eval_js.name: browser_eval_js
browser_eval_js.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the page context and return the result. Use for one-off custom DOM queries or actions. Note: do NOT poll repeatedly with this tool to wait for dynamic page changes; use browser_wait_for(expression=...) instead.

run_deep_linter.name: run_deep_linter
run_deep_linter.description: Run a deep static analysis (Pylint) on a file or directory. This is a heavy operation (~5-10s) but it catches complex issues like shadowing, unused variables, and control flow errors that fast AST linters miss. Use this when you've finished major architectural changes or if you suspect hidden bugs.

check_code.name: check_code
check_code.description: Check code for errors and warnings using the Language Server Protocol (LSP). Returns instant diagnostics (errors, warnings) for a file. Works with Python, C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Java, C++, Ruby, Kotlin, PHP, Dart. Requires the multilspy package (pip install multilspy).

find_implementations.name: find_implementations
find_implementations.description: Find implementations of an interface, abstract class, or method at a specific line and column using LSP.

search_workspace_symbols.name: search_workspace_symbols
search_workspace_symbols.description: Search for symbols (classes, methods, functions, variables) across the entire workspace/project matching a query string using LSP.

get_call_hierarchy.name: get_call_hierarchy
get_call_hierarchy.description: Get the call hierarchy (callers or callees) for a function or method at a specific line and column using LSP.

filter_new_items.name: filter_new_items
filter_new_items.description: Filter a list of items (URLs, IDs, or titles) to return only those not previously reported by this automated or monitoring task.

unity_bake_lightmap.name: unity_bake_lightmap
unity_bake_lightmap.description: Bake lighting and lightmaps for the active Unity 3D scene.
